explanation: Fires on content tokens inside technical or domain compound terms, such as database/programming API words (get_where, failover, sort, output, partitioned by, table) and scientific or legal terms (quantum Hall, topological, emotional distress, Denial of Service). The examples share no clear single trigger; weak firing falls on ordinary function words.

A mixture with two main clusters. It fires on interior subword pieces of biomedical and drug names (Th-al-assaemia, ritux-im-ab, s-ert-indole) and on commas in drug lists. It also fires on auxiliary or function words in Scandinavian, French and German news text (som ble, som har, sont, immer).

Heterogeneous. It fires on tokens such as 'Files' in 'C:\Program Files', 'typename' in C++ templates, 'Bean' in @ManagedBean and 'cDNA', and on the second word of descriptive compounds (television studio, 3D rendering, editing sessions, social butterfly). No common rule predicts it.

Fires mainly on the first subword token of a surname or name, after a first name or initial, especially a capital ' K' (Klobuchar, Knaus, Kiker, Kuhn, KRAUSE). It also fires on interior pieces of words in Danish, Hungarian and Swedish text. Common words like 'are' or 'has' give only weak to mid firing.

Fires on syntactic connector tokens in code and config: ':', ')', '://', '("', ' =', '(', and in Elixir and AWS ARN syntax. It also fires on the space before a number in an enumerated list of numbers or percentages in prose (0, 2.5, 5, [ ]10). These are two loosely related syntax-position behaviours.

Fires on connective tokens inside location, affiliation or range descriptors: 'of' in 'city of'/'west of', commas after a university or hospital name, the space before the upper number in 'aged 9 and 20' or '0 to 21', and 'and' in 'lakes and streams'. It also fires on scattered tokens in names and paths, so the overall picture is a loose mixture.

Fires most consistently on the opening '(' plus variable of a math function definition such as 'Let j(v)', 'g(u)', 'f(x)'. Many top examples are unrelated: subword pieces of rare words (cod-ility, A-iley, Vic-sek, kim-ono), citation tags '@B', and code identifiers.

Fires on the first subword fragment of a long or rare word that the tokenizer splits into pieces. Examples are chemical and medical terms (is-oproterenol, en-graft, en-ucleated, e-icosapentaenoic, en-antioenriched, cre-atinine) and proper names (Ste-ibel, F-rontera, Ch-il-licothe). Whole common words do not trigger it.

A mixture. It fires strongly on '======' separator lines in Hacker News comment dumps, on newlines or spaces after legal or list headers ('1 of 1'), and on code tokens such as '.length', '.RowCount' and ' <' in for-loops. It also fires on scattered biomedical tokens.

Fires on non-initial tokens of proper names: the second word or later subword of person names, place names and organisation names (E-ves-ham, Od-isha, Elizabeth Warren, All Saints Church, Martin Luther King, Atomic Energy, Investor Protection). Firing is strongest for the continuation of a geographic or person name and weak on ordinary words.

Heterogeneous. It fires on 'subject' in PHP license headers ('This source file is subject to'), Java generics commas, '$' in bcrypt hashes, mid-word medical pieces (contrain-dic-ations), and website boilerplate ('Thanks for visiting', 'send a link to'). No single feature is shared.

Fires on the word that completes or continues a fixed multiword expression or collocation, such as 'one way or another', 'in at least one direction', 'in order to', 'in light of', 'people with the surname', 'found the right place', 'just a few'. Context decides it: the same token outside an idiom gives little firing.

No coherent pattern. It fires on varied tokens: 'Smart' in product names, subword pieces of technical terms (dis-engagement, anter-op-osterior), dictionary keys in code ('class', options:), and pieces of proper names (Sk-ins, Burn-el, L'Ch-aim).

Fires mainly on boilerplate in GPL and BSD license headers (the street-number digit in '51 Franklin Street' or '675 Mass Ave', 'that', 'the', ',' in 'write to the Free Software Foundation'). It also fires on the opening of quoted attribute or string values in code (=", '&', "&"), and on acronym pieces inside parentheses (ICD, RSV).
